title: security: rbac v2 - enforce KMS region residency and audit logging hardening
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Context: Customers in regulated environments require both enforcement of KMS key residency (region pinning) and richer audit evidence when keys are used. This PR hardens RBAC v2 to add an enforceable KMS region-residency policy, augments audit logging with explicit region/residency_reason fields, and wires enforcement into the private installer and policy evaluation path. Motivation: previously we only had an audit-only mode and disparate enforcement points across services; this causes gaps for Private deployments and makes compliance attestations harder. Summary of changes: 1) New RBAC policy rules: kms.residency.enforce and kms.residency.admin to allow configuration and emergency overrides. 2) Enforcement path: policy evaluation added to the KMS facade used by the serving runtime and private installer so create/decrypt/copy operations validate region pins. 3) Audit logging: added region, residency_policy_id, residency_verdict (allowed/denied/audit) to KMS audit events and propagated to centralized audit pipeline (audit-collector -> kafka -> audit-store). 4) Migration: a one-time data-backfill script to tag existing KMS events with inferred region when available; also a feature-flag gate (rbac_v2_kms_residency_enforce) that defaults to off for safety and is turned on via release task. 5) Tests and docs: integration tests covering allowed/denied flows, simulator harness for private installer, and docs for operators. Backwards compatibility: default is audit-only (flag off). Enabling enforcement requires a coordinated rollout documented in the migration section. Checklist: - [x] Policy schema added and validated - [x] Enforcement wired at KMS facade - [x] Audit schema and KCL pipeline updated - [x] E2E tests (private + hosted mock) - [x] Migration scripts + rollout guide - [x] Security review and threat modeling Notes for operators: 1) Before enabling enforcement, run the provided dry-run script in a staging environment to surface deny candidates. 2) We recommend creating kms.residency.admin role for emergency overrides confined to a small ops group. Linear/Jira: ENG-4521 tracks policy design; SEC-312 for threat modelling; SUP-2213 contains customer requests and support cases. Rollback: toggle the feature flag off; the enforcement can be bypassed by creating an explicit allowance policy for specific service principals if urgent.
